findings.description: The interval between completed executions has no defined start for a task that never completes its first execution. STK-SUP-001 calls for detecting when any supervised task stops running.
findings.requested_change: Define when alive supervision starts and which event starts the deadline for the first completion.

findings.description: The trigger is a late start, so the requirement permits waiting for the task to start before detecting the fault. A task may remain unstarted after its configured limit while the whole-reaction budget in STK-SUP-009 runs out.
findings.requested_change: Define when a missed activation becomes a late-activation fault while the task is still unstarted, and relate that point to the reaction deadline.

findings.description: The wording 'lasts longer' leaves it unclear whether the configured limit in STK-SUP-002 applies to elapsed time or processor execution time, and whether an overrun is detected while the execution is still in progress.
findings.requested_change: Define what time counts toward the limit, the events used to measure it, and when an ongoing execution must be declared overdue.

findings.description: STK-SUP-003 requires checking order within one control cycle. With task periods of 10 ms and 100 ms in CON-SUP-006, the same execution sequence can be judged differently depending on how the verifier groups activations into cycles. OP-SYS-009 leaves that rule open.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-009 and reference a definition of cycle boundaries, expected activation instances across both rates, and the execution events whose order is checked.

findings.description: Under STK-SUP-003, a skipped task can be judged only once the expected activation and its due point are known. OP-SYS-009 leaves both the cycle boundary and how the 10 ms and 100 ms activations fit into the cycle unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define which task instances are required in each cycle and the event or cutoff at which a missing instance must be reported as skipped.

findings.description: The configured timeout has no stated reference for the first unserviced interval. Under STK-SUP-005, a controller that fails before its first watchdog service still needs the hardware reset fallback. OP-SYS-004 also leaves the timeout setting unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define when the first timeout interval begins, what restarts it after valid service, and which approved timeout setting or range applies.

findings.description: The early-service reset required by STK-SUP-006 is judged against a configured opening. OP-SYS-004 leaves the opening undefined, and the item gives no reference event from which a tester can place an early service attempt for start-up or subsequent windows.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved window-opening configuration and timing origin, and define the reset trigger in terms of the service attempt so it can be tested even when the attempt is rejected.

findings.description: The late-service reset required by STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006 depends on a window closing that OP-SYS-004 does not define. The item does not identify the configuration and timing reference needed to judge a missed service in the first or a subsequent window.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved window-closing configuration and the events that start the first and subsequent windows.

findings.description: The guard is the absence of a detected task fault. It permits servicing when task health has yet to be established, including at start-up. STK-SUP-005 permits service only while every supervised task is healthy.
findings.requested_change: Define the configured evidence that qualifies each task as healthy and specify the approved watchdog service condition before initial task health is established.

findings.description: The independent-watchdog timeout and the window-watchdog service window are independently judgeable. A controller can service the independent watchdog correctly and miss the window watchdog deadline while the STK-SUP-005 health condition is satisfied.
findings.requested_change: State separately verifiable service obligations for the two watchdogs and reference the same approved health condition in both.

findings.description: The phrase 'while a fault ... is detected' leaves the duration of the watchdog service inhibit undefined. A brief detection event followed by resumed service could satisfy one reading while defeating the reset fallback in STK-SUP-005.
findings.requested_change: Define when the inhibit starts and which approved state transition, reset, or recovery condition permits servicing again.

findings.description: The item mandates checking program code against a stored reference. STK-SUP-007 specifies the integrity outcome before the application runs and supplies no rationale for requiring this mechanism.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required integrity outcome or cite an approved constraint and rationale for mandating a stored reference.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 requires a start-up program-code integrity check. OP-SYS-012 leaves the covered code and required error-detection capability undefined, so a test cannot establish that the check covers the required program code and corruptions.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved program-code coverage and corruption detection criteria for the start-up check. Keep the unresolved criteria in OP-SYS-012 as needed input.

findings.description: The item mandates checking configuration data against a stored reference. STK-SUP-007 specifies the integrity outcome before the application runs and supplies no rationale for requiring this mechanism.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required integrity outcome or cite an approved constraint and rationale for mandating a stored reference.

findings.description: STK-SUP-007 requires a start-up configuration-data integrity check. OP-SYS-012 leaves the covered configuration data and required error-detection capability undefined, so a test cannot establish that the check detects the required corruptions.
findings.requested_change: Reference the approved configuration-data coverage and corruption detection criteria for the start-up check. Keep the unresolved criteria in OP-SYS-012 as needed input.

findings.description: Completing one full pass while the application runs can satisfy the item. STK-SUP-008 requires the controller to repeat the check in the background throughout operation.
findings.requested_change: Require recurring full checks during operation and define when the first and subsequent passes are due.

findings.description: The item refers to a full-pass time bound recorded in OP-SYS-002, but that open point establishes no bound. OP-SYS-012 also leaves the scope and error-detection capability of the program-code check undefined. These gaps prevent testing the bounded full pass required by STK-SUP-008.
findings.requested_change: Obtain the approved time bound, define its start and end events, and reference the approved code coverage and corruption detection criteria.

findings.description: The item protects only supervised tasks and permits any timing interference that stays within their configured supervision limits. STK-SUP-008 calls for preserving application timing, while STK-SUP-004 allows the supervised task set to be configured. The rationale gives no basis for the narrower scope or interference allowance.
findings.requested_change: Confirm which application tasks must be protected and obtain measurable timing interference criteria for the background check.

findings.description: STK-SUP-009 gives 50 ms from fault to safe state. OP-SYS-003 leaves the starting event undefined by fault type, and OP-SYS-010 leaves the physical output-off condition undefined. A test therefore has no agreed start and stop events for the 50 ms interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the timer start for each fault type and the observable off state for each control output. Account for worst-case detection latency, including the run-time integrity check.

findings.description: The output-off trigger lists task and memory faults only. STK-SUP-009 refers to any preceding detected fault, and STK-SUP-006 explicitly includes early and late watchdog servicing. The item leaves output shutdown unspecified for those events.
findings.requested_change: Resolve how the 50 ms output-off obligation applies to detected watchdog events and reference the approved behavior through watchdog reset.

findings.description: STK-SUP-009 gives 50 ms from fault to safe state. OP-SYS-003 leaves the starting event undefined by fault type, and OP-SYS-010 leaves the observable not-operational signal undefined. A test therefore has no agreed start and stop events for the 50 ms interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the timer start for each fault type and the observable not-operational indication. Account for worst-case detection latency, including the run-time integrity check.

findings.description: The not-operational trigger lists task and memory faults only. STK-SUP-009 refers to any preceding detected fault, and STK-SUP-006 explicitly includes early and late watchdog servicing. The item leaves the status signal unspecified for those events.
findings.requested_change: Resolve how the 50 ms status indication obligation applies to detected watchdog events and reference the approved signal behavior through watchdog reset.

findings.description: The derivation from STK-SUP-007 and STK-SUP-009 requires holding the not-operational indication until both checks pass. The item defines only the end of the hold. OP-SYS-010 leaves the observable indication and behavior during reset and before software starts unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Define the event that starts the hold, the observable signal state, and the board-level behavior required during reset and early start-up.

findings.description: STK-SUP-010 requires recovery by reset after safe-state entry. OP-SYS-005 leaves the time allowed for recovery open, and OP-SYS-004 leaves it unclear whether a watchdog reset satisfies the item or interrupts the required sequence. A test lacks both a completion limit and a way to judge a watchdog reset during recovery.
findings.requested_change: Define the permitted reset paths and observable completion criterion after safe-state entry. Resolve their precedence and coordination with fault reporting.

findings.description: The item references the number of consecutive operating cycles recorded in OP-SYS-001, which provides no number. It also leaves fault equivalence and what ends a consecutive run undefined. A test cannot determine when the latch required by STK-SUP-010 must take effect.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-SYS-001 with an approved threshold, a unit for counting repeated faults, an equivalence rule, and the events that clear the consecutive count.

findings.description: STK-SUP-010 requires the latched safe state to persist until an actual power cycle. The item ends the hold on the next power-on reset, but the inputs establish no equivalence between that reset classification and a power cycle. Watchdog reset remains possible under the behavior recorded in OP-SYS-004.
findings.requested_change: Define the approved power-cycle release condition and the required continuity of the safe state across resets that occur without a power cycle.

findings.description: The item forces any reset into exactly one of three classes. STK-SUP-011 requires distinguishing those three causes, and OP-SYS-008 leaves other supported reset causes unresolved. If another cause is possible, the item requires an unsupported classification.
findings.requested_change: Confirm the supported reset causes and define the required classification for causes whose treatment STK-SUP-011 leaves open.

findings.description: STK-SUP-011 requires the controller to distinguish reset causes after restart. The stated test can induce a reset but has no specified observation point or time for reading the resulting classification. OP-SYS-008 records this gap.
findings.requested_change: Specify where and when the classification can be observed for verification after each supported reset.

findings.description: STK-SUP-012 requires reporting every detected fault. The trigger covers task and memory faults, while STK-SUP-006 also identifies early and late watchdog servicing as detectable events. The item leaves their reporting, including after restart, unspecified.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the reporting scope for detected watchdog events and specify the applicable report fields and timing.

findings.description: The item requires transmission after detection, but SYS-REC-001 and the watchdogs may reset the controller before transmission finishes. OP-SYS-004 and OP-SYS-005 leave the order open, so the item gives no required outcome for an interrupted report under STK-SUP-012.
findings.requested_change: Define when a report must be fully transmitted relative to supervisor and watchdog resets and how reporting is completed if a reset intervenes.

findings.description: STK-SUP-012 requires a fault code, the affected task or memory area, and a timestamp. OP-SYS-006 leaves the report format, code mapping, and time reference open. The item also leaves the affected-task field undefined for faults involving multiple tasks in an execution sequence.
findings.requested_change: Reference an approved report contract covering encoding, fault and affected-entity mappings, and the timestamp event, reference, and resolution.

findings.description: STK-SUP-013 requires the service tool to read current supervision status. OP-SYS-006 and OP-SYS-007 leave the valid request, expected response content, and response timing undefined. A test cannot determine whether the response represents the current status.
findings.requested_change: Reference the service interface that defines the request and response, required status fields, when the reported status is sampled, and the response time criterion.

findings.description: STK-SUP-013 requires the service tool to read the last faults. OP-SYS-007 gives no retained-fault count or reset retention rule, and 'up to' allows returning fewer reports even when more are available. A test cannot determine the expected result.
findings.requested_change: Define the request and response, the required number and recency of reports to return when records are available, and the retention behavior across resets.

findings.description: The guard includes any time with no detected fault and no safe state, which can include start-up integrity checks. STK-SUP-014 applies the 10% processor-time limit in normal operation, and the rationale provides no basis for extending it to those start-up activities.
findings.requested_change: Define the operating modes and workload that constitute normal operation for the 10% limit.

findings.description: OP-SYS-011 leaves the averaging window and reference clock open. For the STK-SUP-014 limit, an analysis can reach different verdicts depending on the measurement window, which activities count toward supervisor use, and which processor-time denominator is used.
findings.requested_change: Define the measurement window, time reference, included activities, and denominator. Specify how the analysis establishes processor-time use with the verification platform in CON-SUP-005.

findings.description: STK-SUP-015 calls for simulator injection of each preceding fault. The item lists task and integrity-check failures and omits the watchdog timing failures identified in STK-SUP-005 and STK-SUP-006.
findings.requested_change: Include simulator cases that exercise independent-watchdog expiry and early and late window-watchdog service, or record an approved decision on their scope.

findings.description: The item permits injecting a failed integrity-check result. That can exercise the fault response while bypassing detection of code or configuration corruption, which is part of the supervisor behavior STK-SUP-015 calls for testing on a simulator.
findings.requested_change: Specify simulator stimuli and observable outcomes sufficient to demonstrate that the start-up and run-time checks detect the required corruptions.
